sentences.text: This petition seeking quashing of the charge sheet arises out of a matrimonial dispute.
The police have filed the charge sheet for offences punishable under Section 498A of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

Case is pending before the 37th Additional CMM Court, Bengaluru,
in C.C.No.21142/2021.
2.
Petitioners are the husband and in-laws of respondent No.2/complainant.
Petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 are present before the Court.

3. A joint memo has been filed, signed by petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2, wherein it is stated that Crl.Misc.No.60/2021 filed before the V MMTC, Bengaluru and MC No.3039/2023 filed before the II Additional Family Court, Bengaluru, are closed.
As per the joint memo, respondent No.2 herein has agreed to NC: 2025:KHC:5722 quash C.C.No.21142/2021 pending before the 37th Additional CMM Court at Bengaluru.

The joint memo reads as under:
1. That 2nd respondent has no objection to quash the charge sheet in No.21142/2021 filed against the petitioners herein pending before 37th Additional CMM Court at Bengaluru.
2. The 1st petitioner herein is agreed to pay a sum of Rs.35 lakhs which was the amount paid by the 2nd respondent towards the purchase of joint property bearing No.Berings Gade 10 ST TV, Hoje Taastrup 2630 Denmark.
3. The 1st petitioner herein handed over all the gold jewels belonging to the 2nd respondent and 2nd respondent has also handed over the gold jewellery of the 1st petitioner.
4.
Both parties are agreed to withdraw the case in Denmark in case no.BS-26175/2023-GLO in respect of joint property in Denmark.
5. The 2nd respondent has agreed to return the house key to the 1st petitioner herein in respect of the joint property situated at Berings Gade 10 ST TV, Hoje Taastrup 2630 Denmark.

sentences.text: Both the parties have no claims against each other in respect of any property or any claim either in Denmark or in India.
7. The 2nd respondent has agreed not to claim any alimony or maintenance from the 1st petitioner either in the present or future and both have no claims against each other.

8. The 1st Petitioner has issued a DD bearing no.514843 of ICICI Bank dated 31/01/2025 for a sum of Rs.35 Lakhs which is in the custody of the 5th MMTC Court at Bangalore and the same shall be honoured and given to the custody of the 2nd respondent after settlement of all the cases.
9. Both the parties agree that a decree of divorce is already granted by the Court in Denmark.

4. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of JITENDRA RAGHUVANSHI AND OTHERS VS.
BABITA RAGHUVANSHI AND ANOTHER

entities.text:
JITENDRA RAGHUVANSHI AND OTHERS VS.
BABITA RAGHUVANSHI AND ANOTHER
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: reported in 2013 (2) Crimes 90 (SC) has held that, the inherent powers of the High Court under Section 482 of Criminal Procedure Code are wide and unfettered.

It is the duty of the Courts to encourage genuine settlements of matrimonial disputes,
NC: 2025:KHC:5722 particularly, when the same are on considerable increase.

Even if the offences are non-compoundable, if they relate to matrimonial disputes and the Court is satisfied that, the parties have settled the same amicably and without any pressure, for the purpose of securing ends of justice, Section 320 of the Code, would not be a bar to the exercise of power of quashing of FIR.

5. In the case of B.S.Joshi vs. State of Haryana reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has upheld the powers of the High Court under Section 482 of the code to quash criminal proceedings, where dispute is of a private nature and a compromise is entered into between the parties who are willing to settle their differences amicably.

entities.text: B.S.Joshi vs. State of Haryana reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. In view of the settlement arrived at by the parties and in the light of the joint memo filed by them,
there is no purpose in keeping the proceedings pending before the trial Court.
This Court finds that the settlement NC: 2025:KHC:5722 is genuine and therefore, to meet the ends of justice, it is just and proper to quash the entire proceedings pending against the petitioners.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER 1.
Petition is allowed.
2. The proceedings/charge sheet in C.C.No.21142/2021 pending before the 37th Additional CMM Court, Bengaluru, is hereby quashed.
3. Pending I.A.1/2023 stands disposed of.
